entities.summary: Themison of Laodicea was a prominent physician and the founder of the Methodic school of medicine. Born in Laodicea, a city in the Roman province of Asia, around 90 BCE, Themison studied medicine under the tutelage of the famous physician Herodicus. He became a renowned physician in his own right, practicing medicine throughout the Mediterranean region and treating prominent figures such as the Roman Emperor Augustus. The Methodic school of medicine, which Themison founded, emphasized the importance of observation, experimentation, and evidence-based medicine. This approach had a significant impact on the development of Western medicine and influenced medical practice for centuries to come. Themison's medical school in Laodicea became a center of learning and innovation, attracting students from all over the ancient world. Despite his significant contributions to the field of medicine, Themison's life and work remain somewhat shadowed by the more famous figures of his time, such as Galen and Hippocrates. Nevertheless, his legacy as a pioneer of evidence-based medicine continues to be celebrated by medical historians and scholars today.
